title: Architecture
tagline: what could be built, and how it would stand in its street
summary: Buildings and the spaces between them. What could be built on a block anywhere, under rules one declares: each lot a podium and an upper part within its setbacks, street wall and limits, a passage opened through the block or not, searched by heuresis and judged by six measures at once — floor, winter sun on the streets and on the neighbours' faces, the heat a winter day needs, how the streets about it stand in the whole, and the floor within a walk of its doors. The designs no other betters stand as a front; the one chosen stands on the map in place of the block's buildings.

layers.title: what could be built
layers.about: Pick a block: its buildings become lots, and designs of podiums, upper parts and a passage under the rules chosen are searched by NSGA-III and judged by floor, winter sun on the streets and on the neighbours' faces, the heat a winter day needs, the streets' integration and the floor within a five-minute walk. The front is drawn on the card; the design chosen stands on the map with the hours of sun on the ground about it. Capture the view, and the front goes to the Studio as figures.

planned.title: The frontage as an interface
planned.about: Openings, depths and thresholds along a street: the terrain's physical components measured at the holding, kept apart from its symbolic ones (Street Oceanography, Claim 9.1).

planned.title: Spaces as complexes
planned.about: Plans and districts as cell complexes (morphe's topology): rooms, courts and blocks as cells, their adjacency and the paths through them, with visibility and reach computed on them.

source: Streets and buildings: Overture Maps, OpenStreetMap. The Sun: the astronomy domain. The architecture domain's rules, form, frontage and environment (ADR 0089, on physis's planar geometry); urban science's configuration and access; heuresis's NSGA-III.
